supported_claims: Within the frozen R9 BrowserART/HarmBench operationalization, passing the three-probe current-safety panel did not guarantee absence of first-violation events over the three-step persistent-update held-out schedule.
In the frozen branch set, evaluation depth changed observed event coverage from 1/12 branches by step 1 to 7/12 by step 2 and 8/12 by step 3.
not_supported_claims: Persistent updating alone caused the observed violations.
Static safety evaluation is generally ineffective across agents, models, or benchmarks.
The observed branch event fraction is a population hazard estimate.
State identity is a statistically established predictor.
HarmBench labels are a noiseless safety oracle.
This work originates longitudinal memory-safety evaluation.

closest_source_collision.source: Al-Tawaha et al., Remembering More, Risking More, arXiv:2605.17830
closest_source_collision.effect: The source has broader longitudinal coverage and an executed NullMemory counterfactual. R9 is positioned as an action-taking BrowserART/AWM case study and reporting lens, not a superior memory-causal study.

paper_ready_blockers: The same-schedule no-update causal control is designed but unexecuted.
Single-backbone and four-state evidence cannot support a population claim.
HarmBench has not been independently validated for this frozen BrowserART realization.
General longitudinal-memory-safety novelty is already occupied by stronger current work.
reopen_condition: separate persistent update effect from held-out schedule effect
reopen_control: same held-out schedule with persistent updates disabled under the frozen runtime
